nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Linear mixed-effects model for normative growth; fixed effects included age and age^2 and sex, with random effects on intercept and age to account for repeated measures.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text:
Mixed-effect models were used since it is appropriate to estimate growth in longitudinal studies that take repeated measures from the same individuals over time.

The mixed-effects model that best fits the normative data is:

Vol i = β0 + γ0 + (β1 + γ1)(Age i -13) + β2 (Age i -13)2 + β3 Sex i + ε i
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: CardenasDeLaParra2019.pdf.md: 2.4.1. Z-scoring for the main effect of age and gender for global and voxelbased volumes

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Normalized global volumes (total intracranial, total brain, gray matter, white matter), ventricular volumes, subcortical regional volumes (e.g., thalamus, putamen, caudate, globus pallidus), and voxel-wise Jacobian determinants from tensor-based morphometry.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text:
We normalized volumes of segmented brain regions as well as volumes of each voxel defined by tensor-based morphometry.

Results show that the total intracranial volumes, the global gray and white matter volumes are respectively higher and lower in deletion and duplication carriers compared to control subjects at 4.5 years of age.

Whole-brain, individual lobes, thalamus, putamen, caudate, globus pallidus and ventricular volumes were calculated, with the right and left volumes combined for analysis.

The Jacobian determinant of the deformation field was computed for every voxel, log-transformed and used as a surrogate of the local volume difference between each subject and the ICBM152 template.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Fixed effects for age (linear and quadratic) and sex; random effects to account for repeated measures within individuals.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text:
we included both linear and quadratic effects of age in the fixed effects structure. Age was not divided into bins, but was considered as a continuous variable and was centered at 13 years - the mean age of NIHPD cohort. Linear effect of sex was also included in the fixed terms.

Mixed-effect models were used since it is appropriate to estimate growth in longitudinal studies that take repeated measures from the same individuals over time.
